answer: Spatial Beacon Relay. Each identity must hold a unique physical relay node that broadcasts a rotating signed beacon; peers confirm receipt only when the signal crosses a distinct attenuation path, so a cloned beacon leaves a detectable echo in the relay log. Nodes earn standing only by sustaining a real coverage footprint, and a lagoon of contested relays voids standing for all claimants. An attacker must acquire and physically co-locate one relay per identity plus a lantern-grade power source, making each fake identity cost hardware, installation, and site access rather than money alone.
